assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 20,000 req/s peak. Streaming is modelled as SEGMENTED delivery (HLS/DASH), which is genuinely request-based: one GET per ~10 s of audio. 80% of requests are audio segments, i.e. ~16,000 segment GET/s, i.e. ~160,000 concurrent listeners

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: The v1 engine is an analytical open-queueing model of REQUEST arrivals. It cannot express a long-lived socket, a bitrate ladder, or per-session state. Segmented delivery is the closest honest shape and is what real players use; a raw-socket progressive-download design would NOT be modelled correctly here

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: CDN hit-rate 97% on audio segments - a music catalogue has an extremely concentrated hot set - so only 3% of segment requests reach the origin store

assumptions.subject: api
assumptions.statement: Control-plane API ~2,000 rps/instance. Only 20% of system traffic touches it at all; the other 80% is served by the CDN and never reaches origin compute. This is the busiest component in the design

assumptions.subject: analytics
assumptions.statement: One play event per playback start, consumed at ~800 events/s per instance (counter updates plus royalty attribution writes)

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The SQL primary is modelled as ONE instance because there is one writer. A Multi-AZ standby is assumed in a real deployment but is NOT modelled as a second instance: it serves no traffic, and the engine would credit it with capacity it does not have. The engine will therefore flag the primary as a single point of failure - that flag is correct about failover, not about capacity.

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: 1.2 PB: ~100M tracks at ~3 encodings x ~4 MB

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: Delivery volume: ~160 KB per 10-second segment (~128 kbps average across the bitrate ladder) x average segment rate

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Monthly usage volumes (egress/storage/requests) are derived from AVERAGE load = peak / 3; capacity and instance counts are sized to PEAK. A single system_rps cannot carry both, so the peak:average ratio is stated here rather than hidden in a volume.

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Delivery egress is priced at the model's single flat internet-egress rate ($0.09/GB, the US first paid tier). At the petabyte-per-month volume this design implies, a real committed CDN contract is roughly 5-10x cheaper, so the egress line is an UPPER BOUND, not a quote. The volume (GB/month) is the engineering claim; the rate is not negotiated here. For a music service this line is the ENTIRE bill's shape: compute is under 1% of it. That conclusion is robust to the rate; the absolute figure is not

assumptions.subject: scope
assumptions.statement: Recommendations/ML ranking, DRM key serving, offline sync and the ad platform are OUT of this reference

_library.summary: Segmented audio streaming with a CDN-dominated delivery path and a play-event pipeline.
